$comment: Artifact vocabulary for the operational-process corpus (founder depth wave part 2, 2026-10-01): the canonical business artifacts that flow between processes. Each artifact names its one canonical producer process (producedBy); documented exceptions (a second committed process that genuinely also brings the artifact into existence - the LLC route's EIN, the conversion's re-issued charter paper) live in alsoProducedBy. terminal=true marks artifacts no committed process consumes (filed 83(b)s, the dissolution certificate) - everything else is consumed by at least one other process's requires, and every artifact is produced by a committed step (the producer task carries it in produces, pinned to the node where it comes into existence via producesArtifact). No invented artifacts: the registry is sized from the corpus itself. Optional `documents` (founder 2026-10-06, classic document objects): the open-documents/registry.json ids whose registered template genuinely IS this artifact's form (the filed 83(b)'s IRS Form 15620, the executed SAFE's YC forms) - deliberately sparse, honest absence for everything with no registered template; referential integrity tested in lib/__tests__/processArtifacts.test.ts. Optional `geo` (founder geo-coverage ask 2026-10-07): per-country analogs of a US-centric artifact for the six covered countries (UK/IN/DE/FR/PT/CA) - the corpus geoNotes vocabulary (kind analog/absorbed/not-applicable) plus a `label` naming the artifact-level analog object (the EIN's UK analog is the UTR). Derived from the producing process's committed geoNotes; every actionUrl is reused from a committed corpus geoNote (never fresh - tested in lib/__tests__/processArtifacts.test.ts). Kind reads at the artifact level, which can differ from the process note's kind (the UK 'Get EIN' process is absorbed, the UTR object is the analog). Artifacts of global-scope producers carry no geo - the object is the same everywhere. Read back by lib/processes.ts loadArtifacts(); the cross-process dependency graph builds in lib/processDeps.ts; schema: schemas/process-artifacts.schema.json.

artifacts.label: Company name
artifacts.description: The chosen company/brand name - picked from ranked candidates checked against domains, social handles, and trademark conflicts. Feeds the incorporation name check, domain search, trademark filing, and brand monitoring.

artifacts.label: Brand logo
artifacts.description: The primary company logo, generated and set for the chosen brand. Used by the website, the trademark filing, launch assets, and the app-store listings.

artifacts.label: Brand color palette
artifacts.description: The brand color palette, contrast-checked and set as design tokens. Consumed when the company website is generated.

artifacts.label: Domain shortlist
artifacts.description: Ranked available domain candidates with pricing and renewal costs, with matching social handles checked. The input to the actual domain purchase.

artifacts.label: Registered domain
artifacts.description: The company's registered domain name. Everything on the company's own address hangs off it: the email workspace, DNS records, the website, email routing, and the status page.

artifacts.label: DNS control
artifacts.description: Working control of the domain's DNS zone (provisioned with SSL at purchase) - the ability to add the TXT, MX, SPF, and CNAME records that domain verification, email sending, and routing demand.

artifacts.label: Registered agent
artifacts.description: A designated registered agent in the state of incorporation - the legal-documents recipient every state filing names, required before the incorporation filing itself.

geo.label: Registered office (INC-22)
geo.summary: No agent industry: the analog is the registered office itself — declared at (or within 30 days of) incorporation via form INC-22 to the MCA, with the company name displayed at the premises.

geo.label: Registered office (appropriate address)
geo.summary: The analog is the registered office: since the 2023 ECCT Act it must be an 'appropriate address' where documents reliably reach the company, plus a registered email — agent-provided addresses remain fine.

geo.label: Inländische Geschäftsanschrift
geo.summary: No registered-agent concept: the GmbH registers a domestic business address in the Handelsregister where service of process is valid — kept current via the notary.

geo.label: Siège social
geo.summary: The analog is the siège social declared through the guichet unique — the founder's home or a domiciliation company (which must hold a prefectural agrément).

geo.label: Sede
geo.summary: No registered-agent industry: the sede (registered office) is declared at formation in the commercial registry and service of process reaches the company there.

geo.label: Registered office
geo.summary: No registered-agent industry: the registered office address is declared in the articles filed with Corporations Canada (or the provincial registry) and must stay current.

artifacts.label: Certificate of Incorporation
artifacts.description: The state-stamped Certificate of Incorporation - proof the C-Corp exists. The EIN application, bank KYC, state registrations, annual filings, the data room, and ultimately the dissolution all consume it.

geo.label: Certificate of incorporation (Companies House)
geo.summary: Companies House issues the certificate of incorporation when the private limited company registers — online filings are usually approved within 24 hours.
geo.actionLabel: Companies House — set up a limited company

geo.label: SPICe+ certificate of incorporation
geo.summary: The Registrar of Companies issues the certificate of incorporation on the MCA's SPICe+ filing — PAN, TAN and the statutory registrations arrive with it.

geo.label: Handelsregister registration (HRB entry)
geo.summary: The GmbH or UG exists on registration in the Handelsregister after the notarized formation deed; the register excerpt is the company's proof-of-existence paper.

geo.label: RCS registration (extrait Kbis)
geo.summary: Registration through the INPI guichet unique lands the SAS/SASU in the RCS; the Kbis extract is the company's proof of existence.

geo.label: Registo comercial (certidão permanente)
geo.summary: Empresa Online registration creates the Lda or SA in the commercial registry — the NIPC arrives with the registration, and the certidão permanente is the live registry certificate.

geo.label: CBCA certificate of incorporation
geo.summary: Corporations Canada issues the certificate of incorporation on the CBCA filing (often same-day); non-resident founders often incorporate provincially instead because of the federal director-residency rule.

artifacts.label: Bylaws & initial board consent
artifacts.description: The signed bylaws and initial board consent - the company's internal operating rules and first corporate act. A charter document every diligence data room carries.

geo.label: Articles of association
geo.summary: The internal constitution is the articles of association — the statutory model articles apply by default and bespoke articles replace them (there is no separate bylaws document).

geo.label: Memorandum & articles of association (MoA/AoA)
geo.summary: The constitutional documents are the memorandum and articles of association, filed electronically as part of the SPICe+ incorporation.

geo.label: Gesellschaftsvertrag (Satzung)
geo.summary: The company constitution is the Gesellschaftsvertrag inside the notarized formation deed — amendments go back through the notary to the Handelsregister.

geo.label: Statuts
geo.summary: The statuts adopted at formation are the constitutional document, filed through the INPI guichet unique — changing them is a formal amendment.

geo.label: Contrato de sociedade (estatutos)
geo.summary: The contrato de sociedade (the company's estatutos) adopted at formation and registered at the commercial registry is the constitutional document.

geo.label: By-laws & organizational resolutions
geo.summary: CBCA corporations genuinely have by-laws — made by the directors after incorporation and confirmed by shareholders, alongside the organizational resolutions.

artifacts.label: Founder stock issuance
artifacts.description: The signed founder stock purchase agreements - the founders' shares as issued paper. The founding shares entered when the cap table is first set up.

geo.label: Share allotment (SH01 return)
geo.summary: Founder shares are allotted by the company and every allotment is filed at Companies House on the SH01 return within a month.

geo.label: Subscription shares in the MoA
geo.summary: Founders subscribe their initial shares in the memorandum of association as part of the SPICe+ incorporation — no separate issuance step at formation.

geo.label: Gesellschafterliste entry (§ 40 GmbHG)
geo.summary: Founder shares come into existence in the notarized formation deed; the authoritative record is the Gesellschafterliste the notary files in the Handelsregister.

geo.label: Capital subscription in the statuts
geo.summary: Founders' shares are subscribed in the statuts at formation — the capital and holders are part of the registration through the guichet unique.

geo.label: Quota subscription at registration
geo.summary: The founders' quotas and their holders are set in the contrato de sociedade registered through Empresa Online — there is no separate stock-purchase step.

geo.label: Share issuance by directors' resolution
geo.summary: Founder shares are issued by directors' resolution after incorporation under the CBCA, typically at nominal value as part of the organizational resolutions.

artifacts.label: Filed 83(b) election
artifacts.description: The 83(b) election as filed with the IRS within the 30-day window. A terminal tax artifact: nothing downstream consumes it, but the missed window never reopens.

geo.label: Section 431 election
geo.summary: The UK cousin is the joint section 431 ITEPA election to be taxed on the unrestricted value of restricted shares, made within 14 days of acquisition — HMRC's employment-related securities guidance covers it.

geo.label: No 83(b)-style election
geo.summary: Indian tax law has no 83(b)-style election: founder vesting is contractual (reverse vesting mirrored in the articles), and employee share awards are taxed as a perquisite under their own rules.

geo.label: No 83(b) analog (§ 19a EStG instead)
geo.summary: No acceleration election exists; the statutory lever for startup employee equity is § 19a EStG's deferred ('dry income') taxation, not a filing-deadline race.

geo.label: No 83(b) analog
geo.summary: No equivalent election: founder and employee equity are taxed under the regimes the BOFiP doctrine governs (BSPCE, free shares), with no filing deadline to race.

geo.label: No 83(b) concept
geo.summary: There is no 83(b) concept to race: vesting is drafted as quota call-option/clawback clauses, and the 2023 startup law defers qualifying option taxation to liquidity instead.

geo.label: No election deadline to beat
geo.summary: Founder shares are issued at nominal value with CCPC tax deferral, so there is no 83(b)-style election deadline to beat.

artifacts.label: LLC Certificate of Formation
artifacts.description: The stamped Certificate of Formation (Articles of Organization accepted) - proof the LLC exists. Consumed when the LLC later converts to a C-Corp.

geo.label: LLP incorporation certificate (FiLLiP)
geo.summary: The Indian analog is the LLP, incorporated with the MCA via the FiLLiP form, with a partner-drafted LLP agreement filed within 30 days.

geo.label: LLP registration
geo.summary: The pass-through analog is the LLP registered at Companies House — though most UK founders just form a private limited company, since there is no US-style LLC.
geo.actionLabel: Set up and run an LLP

geo.label: UG (haftungsbeschränkt) formation
geo.summary: No LLC analog with pass-through: the low-capital route is the UG — a mini-GmbH formable from €1 with a notarized deed.

geo.label: SARL/EURL registration
geo.summary: The closest analog is the SARL (or single-member EURL), formed like every French entity through the INPI guichet unique.

geo.label: Lda formation
geo.summary: No LLC or check-the-box: the everyday small-company form is the Lda, formable online through Empresa Online with quota capital from €1 — corporate tax treatment, not pass-through.

geo.label: No LLC form
geo.summary: Canada has no LLC: corporations are the only limited-liability company form and there is no check-the-box pass-through election.

artifacts.label: LLC operating agreement
artifacts.description: The signed LLC operating agreement governing the members. The members' consent to a later C-Corp conversion runs under it.

geo.label: LLP agreement
geo.summary: The LLP agreement — drafted by the partners and filed with the MCA within 30 days of incorporation — is the operating agreement's direct analog.

geo.label: LLP members' agreement
geo.summary: An LLP's internal deal lives in a members' agreement; without one, the default statutory provisions apply.
geo.actionLabel: Set up and run an LLP

geo.label: Gesellschaftsvertrag (UG/GmbH)
geo.summary: The governing document of the UG/GmbH route is the notarized Gesellschaftsvertrag — the formation deed carries the internal rules.

geo.label: Statuts de SARL
geo.summary: The SARL's statuts are statute-driven and carry the internal rules — the SARL is a more codified vehicle than a US LLC's freely drafted operating agreement.

geo.label: Contrato de sociedade (Lda)
geo.summary: The Lda's contrato de sociedade carries the internal rules, registered at formation through Empresa Online.

geo.label: No LLC form
geo.summary: With no LLC form in Canada there is no operating agreement to draft — corporations use by-laws and shareholder agreements instead.

artifacts.label: Founder agreement & IP assignment
artifacts.description: The signed founder agreements with IP assignment - the equity split and vesting on paper. Consumed by the cap-table audit and by accelerator applications that ask who owns what.

geo.label: Founders' agreement (stamped)
geo.summary: The founders' agreement is enforceable contract law — but it must be properly stamped to be usable in court, with transfer restrictions and reverse vesting mirrored in the articles.

geo.label: Shareholders' agreement + bespoke articles
geo.summary: Vesting is not a default: it lives in a shareholders' agreement plus bespoke articles, with compulsory-transfer 'leaver' clauses on founder shares.

geo.label: Gesellschaftervereinbarung (notarized options)
geo.summary: GmbH shares only move by notarial deed, so founder vesting is drafted as notarized call-option/clawback clauses in the Gesellschaftervereinbarung.

geo.label: Pacte d'associés
geo.summary: The founder agreement is the pacte d'associés — a private contract alongside the statuts, with vesting built from promesses de cession (share-transfer promises).

geo.label: Acordo parassocial
geo.summary: The split lives in an acordo parassocial with vesting drafted as quota call-option/clawback clauses — quota transfers need written form and registry filing but no notary.

geo.label: Unanimous shareholder agreement
geo.summary: Founders sign a unanimous shareholder agreement (a CBCA creature) with reverse-vesting on founder shares.

artifacts.label: EIN
artifacts.description: The company's federal Employer Identification Number from the IRS. Bank accounts, payroll, state tax registrations, payment processors, insurance applications, and the federal return all require it.

geo.label: UTR (Unique Taxpayer Reference)
geo.summary: The analog identifier is the UTR: HMRC posts it automatically after incorporation (no application), and it anchors the company's Corporation Tax registration.

geo.label: PAN & TAN (via SPICe+)
geo.summary: PAN and TAN — the company's tax identifiers — are allotted automatically as part of the SPICe+ incorporation filing; the Income Tax e-filing portal is where the company then uses them.

geo.label: Steuernummer (ELSTER registration)
geo.summary: The tax office issues a Steuernummer after the Fragebogen zur steuerlichen Erfassung is filed on ELSTER — plus a separate VAT ID from the BZSt if needed.

geo.label: SIREN/SIRET (INSEE)
geo.summary: No application: INSEE allots the SIREN and per-establishment SIRET automatically when the guichet unique registration lands.

geo.label: NIPC (doubles as the tax number)
geo.summary: No separate tax-ID application: the NIPC issued at incorporation is the company's tax number, activated for corporate tax and VAT by the declaração de início de atividade.

geo.label: CRA business number
geo.summary: A CRA business number is issued automatically with federal (and most provincial) incorporation — program accounts (payroll, GST/HST, corporate tax) are added to it rather than applied for separately.

artifacts.label: Business mailing address
artifacts.description: The company's business mailing address (virtual mailbox with the notarized USPS 1583 done). Insurance applications and other provider KYC ask for it.

geo.label: Registered office address
geo.summary: Virtual-office addresses are a normal, legal registered-office choice — post-ECCT the address must be one where documents actually come to the company's attention, plus a registered email address.

geo.label: Registered office (INC-22 filings)
geo.summary: The registered office is declared to the MCA and every change files back to the RoC; virtual-office addresses are widely used, including per-state for GST registrations.

geo.label: Geschäftsanschrift (Handelsregister + Impressum)
geo.summary: The company's domestic business address lives in the Handelsregister and the website's Impressum needs a serviceable address — a business-center address is fine if post genuinely reaches you.

geo.label: Domiciliation (siège social)
geo.summary: Domiciliation is its own regulated service: a prefecture-approved société de domiciliation hosts the siège social, and the address flows through the guichet unique onto the RCS.

geo.label: Sede (registered address)
geo.summary: The sede registered in the commercial registry is where official mail and service arrive — a business-center or virtual-office address is legitimate if post genuinely reaches the company.

geo.label: Registered office street address
geo.summary: The registered office must be a street address in the incorporating jurisdiction where documents can be served — virtual-office providers are a normal choice, with changes filed online.

artifacts.label: Business bank account
artifacts.description: The company's business checking account. The money rail every finance process reads or moves: runway, bill pay, wires, bookkeeping, payroll funding, and the raise's incoming wires.

artifacts.label: Corporate card
artifacts.description: The corporate card program for company spend, synced into the books. Expense management configures its per-employee limits.

artifacts.label: Accounting ledger
artifacts.description: The configured accounting system - chart of accounts with bank and card feeds connected. The books every close, report, budget, and tax filing read.

artifacts.label: Financial statements
artifacts.description: The closed-books P&L and balance sheet from the monthly close. The 409A, the data room, the federal return, and the annual budget consume them.

artifacts.label: Cap table
artifacts.description: The live capitalization table - founding shares, SAFEs, and grants recorded. Read by the 409A, option grants, the data room, the raise, the SAFE conversion, franchise tax, and the pre-raise audit.

artifacts.label: Payment processor account
artifacts.description: The activated payment processor account with API keys integrated and payouts confirmed. Billing, invoicing, refunds, revenue reporting, promo codes, and the sales-tax nexus study all run through it.

artifacts.label: Subscription billing
artifacts.description: Configured subscription plans, customer portal, webhooks, and dunning on the payment processor. Pricing changes, churn saves, and win-back campaigns operate on it.

artifacts.label: State tax accounts
artifacts.description: The state tax registration numbers (income, employment, sales where applicable) in operating states. Payroll setup files employment taxes against them.

geo.label: Per-state GST & professional-tax registrations
geo.summary: The state layer is real here: GST registration is per state of operation, and professional tax plus shops-and-establishments registration are state acts.

geo.label: National HMRC registrations
geo.summary: No states: registering for taxes means one national HMRC registration each — Corporation Tax, PAYE when you employ, and VAT past the threshold.

geo.label: Gewerbeanmeldung (municipal)
geo.summary: The sub-national layer is municipal: a Gewerbeanmeldung with each municipality you operate in, which drives Gewerbesteuer at that municipality's rate.

geo.label: National registrations (CFE assessed automatically)
geo.summary: Registrations are national and flow from the guichet unique filing; local business taxes (the CFE) are then assessed per commune automatically.

geo.label: Início de atividade + Segurança Social
geo.summary: One national layer instead of states: the início de atividade declaration covers corporate tax and VAT in one filing, with Segurança Social employer registration as the second rail.
geo.actionLabel: Portal das Finanças — início de atividade

geo.label: Provincial tax accounts
geo.summary: The provincial layer is real: GST/HST is federal via the business number, but several provinces run their own PST/QST registrations plus payroll levies and workers'-compensation accounts.

artifacts.label: Sales tax registrations
artifacts.description: Registrations with each state's department of revenue where nexus thresholds are crossed, with collection and automated filings enabled. Terminal: the platform remits on schedule.

geo.label: GST registration
geo.summary: GST replaces the per-state sales-tax patchwork with one national regime — registration per state of operation on the GST portal; foreign SaaS falls under the OIDAR rules.

geo.label: VAT registration
geo.summary: Instead of per-state sales tax there is one national VAT registration — mandatory past the turnover threshold — with returns filed digitally under Making Tax Digital.

geo.label: VAT registration + BZSt VAT ID
geo.summary: One German VAT registration covers the whole country; for EU-wide B2C digital sales a single OSS (One-Stop-Shop) return replaces per-country registrations.

geo.label: TVA registration
geo.summary: One national TVA registration replaces the state-by-state patchwork — declared and paid through the espace professionnel, with OSS covering EU-wide B2C digital sales.

geo.label: IVA registration
geo.summary: One national VAT registration (activated by the início de atividade declaration) replaces per-state registrations, with OSS consolidating EU-wide B2C digital sales.

geo.label: GST/HST + provincial registrations
geo.summary: Genuinely nexus-like: register for GST/HST once worldwide taxable supplies pass the small-supplier threshold, then layer the separate provincial registrations where your customers are.

artifacts.label: Foreign qualifications
artifacts.description: Foreign-qualification filings in states with employees or offices. Withdrawn one by one when the company shuts down.

geo.label: Per-state registrations (GST et al.)
geo.summary: Employees or premises in a new state typically mean a fresh GST registration for that state, plus state professional tax and a shops-and-establishments registration.

geo.label: No intra-UK qualification
geo.summary: Inside the UK there is nothing to qualify for; the concept appears at the border — a foreign company opening a UK establishment registers it with form OS IN01.

geo.label: Per-municipality Gewerbeanmeldung
geo.summary: The analog is municipal: each additional Betriebsstätte needs its own Gewerbeanmeldung with that municipality, and Gewerbesteuer is apportioned across them.

geo.label: Établissement secondaire (per-establishment SIRET)
geo.summary: A new office is an établissement secondaire declared through the guichet unique, which issues a per-establishment SIRET — a formality rather than a qualification battle.

geo.label: No sub-national layer
geo.summary: No sub-national layer to qualify into: one commercial registry and one tax registration cover the whole country — the concept only appears at the border.

geo.label: Extra-provincial registration
geo.summary: The concept genuinely exists: carrying on business in a province means extra-provincial registration there — a federal corporation still registers in each province where it operates.
geo.actionLabel: Register in a province or territory

artifacts.label: Insurance policies
artifacts.description: Bound D&O, E&O, general liability, and cyber coverage. The office lease's certificate-of-insurance requirement draws on it.

artifacts.label: Federal tax return
artifacts.description: The filed federal corporate return (Form 1120). The R&D credit's Form 6765 rides on it.

geo.label: ITR-6 return
geo.summary: Companies file the ITR-6 return electronically on the Income Tax e-filing portal; the tax year runs April–March rather than the calendar year.

geo.label: CT600 Company Tax Return
geo.summary: The company files a CT600 with HMRC within 12 months of its accounting period end — plus statutory accounts to Companies House.

geo.label: Körperschaftsteuer & Gewerbesteuer returns
geo.summary: Corporation tax plus trade tax returns are filed electronically through ELSTER, in practice via a Steuerberater.

geo.label: IS declaration
geo.summary: Corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) is declared and paid through the company's espace professionnel on impots.gouv.fr.

geo.label: Modelo 22 (IRC)
geo.summary: The company files the Modelo 22 (IRC) return electronically through the Portal das Finanças, plus the IES annual declaration — in practice via a certified accountant.

geo.label: T2 corporation income tax return
geo.summary: The company files a T2 return with the CRA within six months of its fiscal year-end, plus any provincial corporate returns outside the CRA-administered provinces.

artifacts.label: Certificate of dissolution
artifacts.description: The accepted certificate of dissolution - the company's legal end. Terminal by definition.

geo.label: STK-2 strike-off / IBC voluntary liquidation
geo.summary: Two exits: MCA strike-off via form STK-2 for a company with no liabilities, or a formal voluntary liquidation under the IBC overseen by the IBBI.

geo.label: DS01 voluntary strike-off
geo.summary: A solvent company applies for voluntary strike-off with a DS01 filing to Companies House (or a members' voluntary liquidation for larger balance sheets).

geo.label: Liquidation & Löschung (Handelsregister)
geo.summary: Winding up a GmbH is slow by design: a notarized dissolution resolution, liquidators registered, creditors invited — then a mandatory one-year Sperrjahr before the company is deleted from the Handelsregister.

geo.label: Dissolution-liquidation, radiation du RCS
geo.summary: The sequence is dissolution, a liquidation phase closing the accounts, then radiation from the RCS — every step filed through the guichet unique.

geo.label: Dissolução e encerramento (registry)
geo.summary: Wind-down runs through the registry's dissolution-and-liquidation channel, plus the final Modelo 22 and IES and the cessação de atividade declarations.

geo.label: Articles of dissolution
geo.summary: A solvent corporation dissolves by shareholder-authorized articles of dissolution filed with Corporations Canada — CRA program accounts close and the final T2 files before the certificate issues.

artifacts.label: Privacy policy
artifacts.description: The published privacy policy (and DPA flow) on the company site. Security questionnaires and app-store privacy labels point at it.

artifacts.label: Terms of Service
artifacts.description: The drafted and counsel-reviewed Terms of Service published to the website. Terminal: customers accept it; no committed process consumes it downstream.

artifacts.label: SaaS agreement template
artifacts.description: The standard SaaS subscription agreement template, counsel-reviewed. The SLA's credit terms get added into it.

artifacts.label: Executed NDA
artifacts.description: A countersigned mutual NDA, filed. Terminal: event paper for one counterparty.

artifacts.label: IP assignments (PIIA)
artifacts.description: Executed proprietary-information and invention-assignment agreements for every founder and employee. Diligence data rooms must carry them.

artifacts.label: Trademark application
artifacts.description: The USPTO trademark application and its serial number, as filed. Terminal: prosecution runs at the USPTO's pace.

geo.label: CGPDTM trade mark application
geo.summary: Trade marks are filed with the Controller General (CGPDTM) through the IP India e-filing portal.

geo.label: UK IPO trade mark application
geo.summary: UK marks are filed online with the UK IPO; since Brexit an EUIPO registration no longer covers the UK, so UK + EU protection means two filings.
geo.actionLabel: UK IPO — register a trade mark

geo.label: DPMA application (or EUIPO)
geo.summary: National marks are filed with the DPMA; the EU-wide alternative is a single EUIPO application covering all 27 member states.

geo.label: INPI dépôt de marque (or EUIPO)
geo.summary: French marks are filed online with the INPI; an EUIPO application is the single-filing route to EU-wide protection.

geo.label: INPI registo de marca (or EUIPO)
geo.summary: National marks are filed online with INPI; PT + EU protection is usually one EUIPO filing covering all member states.

geo.label: CIPO trademark application
geo.summary: File with CIPO (online, Nice-classified, Madrid Protocol available) — and budget for the queue: CIPO examination waits run years, so file early.

artifacts.label: Signed board minutes
artifacts.description: Signed board minutes filed on cadence - the clean corporate record a priced round's diligence reads.

artifacts.label: Board-approved annual budget
artifacts.description: The operating plan and headcount budget the board signed off. Terminal: departments execute against it.

artifacts.label: Company email workspace
artifacts.description: The company email/calendar/docs workspace on the domain. Sending company mail, provisioning hires, routing aliases, the CRM inbox, outbound sequences, and SSO identity all build on it.

artifacts.label: Team chat workspace
artifacts.description: The team chat workspace with default channels. Hiring, offboarding, alerts, approvals, and announcements all land in it.

artifacts.label: Project tracker
artifacts.description: The configured project tracker (teams, workflows, labels). Issues, projects, incident follow-ups, pen-test findings, and OKR key results live in it.

artifacts.label: Team wiki
artifacts.description: The team wiki with meeting notes and process templates. Hypothesis docs, the handbook, board rooms, process docs, and OKR tracking get published into it.

artifacts.label: Document storage
artifacts.description: The shared company document system with its folder structure. The diligence data room is hosted out of it.

artifacts.label: Team password manager
artifacts.description: The team password manager with shared vaults and access groups. Terminal: shared credentials live in it operationally.

artifacts.label: Identity provider (SSO)
artifacts.description: The SSO identity provider tenant with role-based groups and MFA. Hire provisioning (SSO/SCIM), SOC 2 integrations, and quarterly access reviews run through it.

artifacts.label: Device management (MDM)
artifacts.description: The MDM with the fleet enrolled and baseline policies pushed. Terminal: its compliance reports feed SOC 2 evidence continuously.

artifacts.label: Code hosting organization
artifacts.description: The code hosting org with repos, branch protection, and team access. CI, the shipping loop, releases, agent-readiness work, and offboarding's access removal depend on it.

artifacts.label: CI/CD pipeline
artifacts.description: The CI/CD pipeline with test, lint, and deploy jobs. Every feature merge and release cut ships through it.

artifacts.label: Cloud infrastructure
artifacts.description: The production cloud footprint - networking, database, compute, IAM, monitoring. Data-warehouse pipelines and pen-test environments are provisioned from it.

artifacts.label: Company website
artifacts.description: The published company website. Policies, content, pricing pages, signup forms, support widgets, and the careers page all live on it.

artifacts.label: Error tracking
artifacts.description: Error monitoring with alert rules and release tracking wired to the repo. Release monitoring and on-call alerting consume it.

artifacts.label: Product analytics
artifacts.description: Product analytics with the SDK installed and key events defined. Launch spikes, referral conversion, churn saves, and warehouse event sources read from it.

artifacts.label: Incident platform
artifacts.description: On-call schedules, escalation policies, and incident workflows. Postmortems assemble their timelines from it.

artifacts.label: Status page
artifacts.description: The public status page on the company domain with uptime monitors wired. Postmortem write-ups publish to it.

artifacts.label: Data warehouse & BI
artifacts.description: The data warehouse with pipelines from production systems and BI dashboards. Terminal: reporting reads it operationally.

artifacts.label: CRM
artifacts.description: The CRM with pipeline, properties, and the email inbox connected. Outbound lists, health scores, and win-back logging live in it.

artifacts.label: Transactional email
artifacts.description: The transactional email account with the sending domain authenticated. Terminal: the product sends receipts and resets through it.

artifacts.label: Marketing email audience
artifacts.description: The email marketing audience with templates and welcome automation. Referral announcements and win-back sequences send to it.

artifacts.label: Customer support desk
artifacts.description: The support platform with messenger widget, inbox routing, and help center. Terminal: customer conversations flow through it operationally.

artifacts.label: Diligence data room
artifacts.description: The permissioned investor data room - charter docs, cap table, financials, contracts, kept current. Board minutes file into it; the priced round's diligence runs on it.

artifacts.label: Executed SAFEs
artifacts.description: Signed SAFE notes with wires verified - the pre-seed on paper. Cap-table updates, the pre-raise audit, and the priced-round conversion consume them.

geo.label: iSAFE / CCPS / CCD instruments
geo.summary: Pre-seed runs on CCPS/CCD instruments or the iSAFE — a practitioner adaptation of the SAFE onto compulsorily convertible preference shares.

geo.label: ASA (advanced subscription agreement)
geo.summary: The SAFE analog is the ASA or convertible loan note — with the round really driven by SEIS/EIS tax relief and its advance-assurance and longstop-date constraints.

geo.label: Wandeldarlehen (convertible loan)
geo.summary: Pre-seed runs on the Wandeldarlehen, kept notarization-free in most setups; angels claim the federal INVEST grant on qualifying equity tickets.

geo.label: BSA-AIR
geo.summary: The SAFE analog is the BSA-AIR (bon de souscription d'actions — accord d'investissement rapide), a practitioner-standard warrant instrument.

geo.label: Convertible loan note
geo.summary: Pre-seed runs on convertible loan notes rather than SAFEs, with the Programa Semente deduction as the angel-side incentive.

geo.label: SAFE under NI 45-106 exemptions
geo.summary: SAFEs are used in Canadian pre-seeds, but securities law is provincial: issuances ride NI 45-106 prospectus exemptions with a report of exempt distribution after closing.

artifacts.label: Priced round closing
artifacts.description: The closed priced round - consents signed, closing packet executed, wires verified, shares issued. The trigger for every outstanding SAFE's conversion.

geo.label: Private placement (s.42, PAS-3)
geo.summary: A priced round is a private placement under Companies Act s.42: special resolution, registered-valuer report on price, PAS-3 return of allotment, and RBI reporting if the money is foreign.

geo.label: Share allotment + SH01
geo.summary: Closing means allotting new shares: board and shareholder authorities, a subscription and shareholders' agreement, new articles for the preferred class, then the SH01 filed within a month.

geo.label: Notarized Kapitalerhöhung
geo.summary: A priced round is a notarized capital increase: the new shares only exist once the increase is registered in the Handelsregister — notary lead time is part of the closing plan.

geo.label: Augmentation de capital
geo.summary: Closing is an augmentation de capital: an extraordinary general meeting, updated statuts, funds certified on a blocked account, then the capital change filed through the guichet unique.

geo.label: Aumento de capital
geo.summary: A priced round is a shareholder-resolved aumento de capital registered at the commercial registry — notarization is generally no longer required for standard increases.

geo.label: Articles of amendment + NI 45-106 placement
geo.summary: Closing means articles of amendment creating the preferred class plus a private placement under NI 45-106 exemptions, with the exempt-distribution report due within 10 days.

artifacts.label: 409A valuation
artifacts.description: The accepted 409A fair-market-value report. Every option grant - including the first hire's - requires a current one.

geo.label: Registered-valuer report (Rule 11UA)
geo.summary: No 409A, but pricing is still regulated: share issues need a report from an IBBI-registered valuer or merchant banker, and ESOP perquisite tax runs off fair market value.

geo.label: EMI valuation agreed with HMRC (VAL231)
geo.summary: The analog is agreeing an EMI valuation with HMRC's Shares and Assets Valuation team: it fixes market value for 90 days, so grants happen inside that window.

geo.label: No statutory appraisal
geo.summary: No 409A equivalent: there is no statutory safe-harbor appraisal for strike prices — pricing is a company-and-tax-advisor judgment, and the statutory lever that matters is § 19a EStG's deferred taxation.

geo.label: No appraisal safe harbor
geo.summary: No 409A equivalent: BSPCE strike prices are set by the issuing company with no statutory appraisal — the BOFiP doctrine governs eligibility and taxation.

geo.label: No appraisal ritual
geo.summary: No 409A ritual: plans are priced by the company and its advisors, and the 2023 startup law defers qualifying option taxation to liquidity instead.

geo.label: No CRA appraisal safe harbor
geo.summary: No 409A equivalent: CRA publishes no appraisal safe harbor — CCPC option rules defer the employee's tax to sale regardless, so the annual-valuation ritual has no counterpart.

artifacts.label: Option grants
artifacts.description: Board-approved, signed, and recorded stock option grants. Offboarding's exercise-window notice runs against them.

geo.label: ESOP grants (s.62(1)(b))
geo.summary: ESOPs need a shareholders' special resolution and are taxed as a perquisite at exercise on a registered valuation — DPIIT-recognised startups can defer that perquisite tax.

geo.label: EMI options
geo.summary: UK startups grant EMI options — an HMRC-approved scheme with capital-gains treatment, valuations agreed with HMRC in advance, and grants notified to HMRC.

geo.label: VSOP / § 19a shares
geo.summary: Most startups grant VSOPs (virtual options, cash-settled); § 19a EStG now defers the dry-income tax on genuine employee shares for qualifying startups.

geo.label: BSPCE
geo.summary: French startups grant BSPCE — founder-company warrants reserved for young companies, with capital-gains-style taxation and no employer social charges.

geo.label: Startup-law option plan (Lei 21/2023)
geo.summary: Options are granted under a company plan with shareholder approval; for recognised startups the Lei 21/2023 regime defers taxation of qualifying plans to liquidity.

geo.label: CCPC stock options
geo.summary: Grants are board-approved under the plan; for CCPCs the employee's taxable benefit is deferred until the shares are sold, with the 110(1)(d) deduction available.

artifacts.label: Signed offer / employment agreement
artifacts.description: The accepted offer letter - an employee on paper. Payroll runs, provisioning, reviews, and offboarding all presuppose it.

geo.label: Appointment letter (+ EPF/ESI setup)
geo.summary: First-hire paper is the appointment letter, alongside EPF/ESI applicability checks, a state shops-and-establishments registration, and monthly TDS on salary.

geo.label: Written statement of particulars
geo.summary: A written statement of particulars is a day-one legal right; gov.uk's first-hire checklist adds right-to-work checks, employers' liability insurance, and PAYE before the first payday.

geo.label: Arbeitsvertrag (NachwG written terms)
geo.summary: The Nachweisgesetz requires the essential terms of employment in writing (tightened in 2022, with fines) — the German employment contract carries them.

geo.label: Contrat de travail + DPAE
geo.summary: Every hire starts with the DPAE to URSSAF before the start date, plus a written contract in French and affiliation to the mandatory mutuelle and retirement schemes.

geo.label: Contrato de trabalho + admissao
geo.summary: The admission is reported to Segurança Social before the start date, mandatory work-accident insurance is taken out, and the written contract terms are put in place.

geo.label: Employment agreement (provincial standards)
geo.summary: The agreement rides the employee's provincial employment-standards minimums, with a payroll (RP) account and workers'-compensation registration before the first payday.

artifacts.label: Contractor record (W-9 on file)
artifacts.description: A payable 1099 contractor in payroll - W-9 and payment details on file. Year-end 1099 filings verify against it.

geo.label: PAN + TDS record
geo.summary: Onboarding a contractor means collecting their PAN and deducting TDS from every payment, deposited monthly and reported quarterly.

geo.label: IR35 status determination (CEST)
geo.summary: Before the contract: an IR35/off-payroll status check — HMRC's CEST tool gives a rulable answer, and misclassification lands the tax bill on you.

geo.label: Status determination (DRV Clearingstelle)
geo.summary: The risk is Scheinselbständigkeit: a one-client contractor working like staff triggers retroactive social contributions — the DRV Clearingstelle runs an official status procedure.

geo.label: URSSAF attestation de vigilance
geo.summary: Contractors must be registered, and for contracts of €5,000+ you must collect and verify their URSSAF attestation de vigilance every six months.

geo.label: Recibos verdes
geo.summary: Contractors invoice through recibos verdes on the tax authority's portal — with reclassification risk (falsos recibos verdes) when the work looks like staff work.

geo.label: RC4110 status determination
geo.summary: Status is decided on CRA's employee-vs-self-employed factors (guide RC4110): misclassify and the employer owes retroactive CPP and EI with penalties.

artifacts.label: Payroll account
artifacts.description: The configured payroll provider - the system of record for paying people and filing employment taxes. Hiring, payroll runs, contractors, the 401(k), visa updates, R&D payroll offset, and the final payroll all run on it.

geo.label: EPF/ESI employer registration
geo.summary: Employer setup spans EPF and ESI registration plus state-level professional tax; salary TDS is deposited monthly against the company's TAN.

geo.label: PAYE employer registration (RTI)
geo.summary: Register as an employer with HMRC for PAYE before the first payday, then report pay through Real Time Information on or before every payment.

geo.label: Betriebsnummer
geo.summary: You need a Betriebsnummer from the Federal Employment Agency before running payroll, then monthly social-insurance reports to each employee's health insurer and wage tax via ELSTER.

geo.label: DPAE + DSN
geo.summary: Every hire starts with a DPAE filed with URSSAF; monthly payroll then flows through the DSN, France's unified payroll report.

geo.label: Segurança Social employer registration
geo.summary: Register as an employer with Segurança Social and report each hire before they start, then file the monthly remuneration declaration and withhold income tax.

geo.label: CRA payroll (RP) account
geo.summary: Open a payroll (RP) program account on the CRA business number before the first remittance, and register with the provincial workers'-compensation board.

artifacts.label: Benefits plan
artifacts.description: The company's enrolled benefits (health, dental, vision) configured in payroll. New-hire enrollment and offboarding termination act on it.

geo.label: Group mediclaim (+ statutory ESI/EPF floor)
geo.summary: The statutory floor is ESI health cover, EPF retirement, and gratuity; on top, a group mediclaim policy is the standard startup benefit.

geo.label: Benefits-in-kind (P11D / payrolling)
geo.summary: The NHS makes health insurance a perk rather than table stakes; the mandatory piece is pension auto-enrolment, and private benefits are taxable benefits-in-kind reported to HMRC.

geo.label: Statutory insurances ride payroll
geo.summary: Health, pension, care and unemployment insurance are statutory and ride payroll — there is no benefits-enrollment project; the discretionary layer is a bAV pension offer and perks.

geo.label: Mutuelle + prévoyance
geo.summary: Every employer must provide a mutuelle — complementary health insurance at least 50% employer-funded — plus prévoyance cover for cadres; both plug into payroll's DSN.

geo.label: Statutory social security + SNS
geo.summary: Statutory social security rides payroll and the SNS provides universal healthcare — there is no benefits-enrollment project; the common extras are meal allowance and private health as perks.

geo.label: Group extended-health benefits
geo.summary: Provincial medicare covers care, so the real project is the extended-health layer: group benefits through an insurer, with CRA's taxable-benefit rules deciding what lands on the T4.

artifacts.label: 401(k) plan
artifacts.description: The adopted retirement plan with the payroll integration connected. Terminal: contributions sync on every payroll run.

geo.label: EPF (Employees' Provident Fund)
geo.summary: The EPF is the mandatory retirement vehicle once headcount crosses 20 — 12% of basic pay from employer and employee each, administered through the EPFO portal.

geo.label: Workplace pension auto-enrolment
geo.summary: Not optional like a 401(k): every UK employer must auto-enrol eligible staff into a workplace pension and declare compliance to The Pensions Regulator.

geo.label: bAV (Entgeltumwandlung)
geo.summary: State pension contributions ride payroll automatically; the 401(k) analog is betriebliche Altersvorsorge — every employer must offer salary conversion with an employer top-up.

geo.label: AGIRC-ARRCO (auto via DSN)
geo.summary: Mandatory complementary pensions enroll automatically through payroll's DSN — nothing to set up; the optional analog is a PER d'entreprise as a perk.

geo.label: State pension via social security
geo.summary: State pension contributions ride the single social-security charge automatically and no occupational plan is mandated — a company PPR is a voluntary perk.

geo.label: Group RRSP / DPSP
geo.summary: CPP rides payroll automatically; the 401(k) analog is the voluntary group RRSP or DPSP most tech employers offer.

artifacts.label: Applicant tracking system
artifacts.description: The ATS with interview stages, postings, and scorecards. The multi-role hiring pipeline is built on top of it.

artifacts.label: Employee handbook
artifacts.description: The published employee handbook - policies, PTO, conduct, remote work, equity. Terminal: the team works under it.

artifacts.label: Office lease
artifacts.description: The signed office lease with deposit wired and certificate of insurance delivered. Terminal: the company occupies under it.

artifacts.label: Compliance platform
artifacts.description: The compliance automation platform with integrations connected. MDM evidence, vendor reviews, and the Type II's continuous monitoring wire into it.

artifacts.label: Security policies
artifacts.description: The reviewed security policy set generated for SOC 2. The policy corpus security questionnaires are answered from.

artifacts.label: SOC 2 Type I report
artifacts.description: The completed SOC 2 Type I audit - the point-in-time snapshot the Type II observation window starts from.

artifacts.label: SOC 2 Type II report
artifacts.description: The SOC 2 Type II report published to the trust center. Terminal: enterprise buyers read it.

artifacts.label: Pen test report & attestation
artifacts.description: The annual penetration test report with retest attestation letter. SOC 2 Type II fieldwork expects it.

artifacts.label: Vendor contract
artifacts.description: A signed vendor agreement from the selection process. Vendor security reviews assess them; shutdown cancels them.

artifacts.label: Fund LP certificate
artifacts.description: The stamped Delaware Certificate of Limited Partnership - the fund vehicle exists. The close runs on it.

artifacts.label: Fund LPA & GP operating agreement
artifacts.description: The signed limited partnership agreement and GP operating agreement. Subscription documents and the close execute under them (amended & restated at close).

artifacts.label: Fund bank account
artifacts.description: The fund's own bank account. Closing wires and capital calls land in it.

artifacts.label: Fund closing
artifacts.description: The held first-and-final close - LP subscriptions signed and the A&R LPA executed with the final LP schedule. Capital calls only exist after it.
